map.An expressions adventure in five chapter: A story about expressions. It has five chapters and six reader gates. Solve the math to move the story.
map.Distortion detected. It is rewriting the: A bad pattern is here. It is changing the city's signs. Reader: get set.
map.Previously, in Volume Five: the crew's b: Last time, in Volume Five: the crew's plans rebuilt the Brightside lot. It got a skate ramp, beds, and a stage. The mayor kept Layla's sketch. Then the new street signs began to talk. They made no sense.
map.Library Lane now says \"⌁§∆!?\". The bak: Library Lane now says "⌁§∆!?". The bake shop sign says it too. EACH sign says it.
map.Distortion source: below the library. So: Source found. It is under the library. It is changing the signs.
map.Ms. Ortiz says Ada Vex built a cipher va: Ms. Ortiz says Ada Vex built a cipher vault. It is under the library. The sign machine is in it.
map.A vault full of locks and puzzles? Crew…: A vault full of locks and puzzles? Crew, I was born for this. Follow me.
map.Under Vexhall Library. A stone stairwell: Under Vexhall Library. It has stone steps. It is dark and deep.
Ms. Ortiz left us two jars of glow ink. Each stair lamp uses one third of a jar.
map.So the question is 2 ÷ 1/3. How many thi: So the question is 2 ÷ 1/3. How many thirds fit in two whole jars?
map.The answer to a division is called the q: The answer to a division problem is the quotient. Draw a bar for each jar. Cut each bar into thirds. Count the parts. Models do not lie.
map.Dividing by a fraction asks \"how many o: Dividing by a fraction asks: how many of that part fit inside? A bar model shows the parts. Cut, then count.
map.Reader — you're our fifth crew member. L: Reader, you are on our crew. Light the stairs!
map.Two jars of glow-ink. Each stair lantern: Two jars of glow ink. Each stair lamp uses 1/3 of a jar. Lock A: how many lamps can the crew light? Find 2 ÷ 1/3. Lock B: the extra 3/4 jar is shared. Each of 3 hand lamps gets the same. Find 3/4 ÷ 3.
map.Conceptual: dividing by 1/3 asks 'how ma: Conceptual: dividing by 1/3 asks how many thirds FIT inside. Count the parts in the bar model. And sharing with 3 lamps makes each share SMALLER.
map.Procedural: Lock A — every jar holds exa: Procedural: Lock A: each jar holds 3 thirds. Count the thirds in BOTH bars. Lock B: dividing by 3 is the same as taking 1/3 of it. Multiply 3/4 × 1/3. Then simplify the fraction.
map.There it is — a scribble made of broken: There it is. A scribble made of broken equations. It just wrote "3⁴ = 12" on the wall.
map.Boss fight, level one. It guards the pow: Boss fight, level one. It guards the power cells. Wrong totals keep the lights off.
map.3⁴ is a power: base 3, exponent 4. The e: 3⁴ is a power. The base is 3. The exponent is 4. The exponent counts the times you multiply the base. It is not base times exponent. The glitch wants you to add or cheat.
map.An exponent is repeated multiplication:: An exponent is repeated multiplication. 5² = 5 × 5, not 5 × 2. Say "three to the fourth power."
map.Charge both cells, reader. Real totals o: Charge both cells, reader. Use true totals. No glitch math.
map.The glitch scrawled “3⁴ = 12” on the wal: The glitch wrote “3⁴ = 12” on the wall. It is wrong. Charge both cells with TRUE totals. Cell A holds 3⁴ gems. Cell B holds 2⁵.
map.Conceptual: the exponent counts how many: Conceptual: the exponent counts copies of the base. You MULTIPLY them. It never multiplies the base by itself. That is the glitch's top trick.
map.Procedural: write it long. 3⁴ = 3 × 3 ×: Procedural: write it out. 3⁴ = 3 × 3 × 3 × 3. Multiply one step at a time, left to right. Then write five 2s for Cell B. Do the same.
map.The sign-press room. A brass machine the: The sign press room. A brass machine as big as a bus. It eats letter tiles.
map.The press only prints when we feed it Ad: The press prints only for Ada's sentence. It must be in symbols, not words.
map.Word-to-code translation. The letter n i: Words to code. The letter n is the variable. It stands for the mystery number.
map.In a term like 7y, the 7 is the coeffici: In a term like 7y, the 7 is the coefficient. It is the number that multiplies the variable. Change the words to math. Then test your expression with a number.
map.An algebraic expression is math with at: An algebraic expression is math. It has at least one variable. "Times" turns into a coefficient. "More than" is addition.
map.Your turn, reader. Build Ada's expressio: Your turn, reader. Build Ada's expression. Then run it.
map.Ada's journal: “5 more than 3 times the: Ada's notes say: “5 more than 3 times the mystery number n.” Step 1: pick the expression that says it in symbols. Step 2: test the press. Evaluate your expression for n = 4.
map.Test-run the press at n = 4. Your expres: Test the press at n = 4. Your expression =
map.Conceptual: '3 times n' builds one multi: Conceptual: "3 times n" makes one term. The 3 is the coefficient. "5 more than THAT" adds 5 to the product. It does not add 5 to n first.
map.Procedural: translate the 'times' part f: Procedural: write the "times" part first. Then add the "more than" part at the end. To evaluate, substitute 4 for n. Multiply BEFORE you add.
map.Twin door rule: each pair only powers up: Twin door rule: a pair powers up only if the sides match. Both must be equivalent expressions. Same value for EACH x.
map.x + x is two sticks taped together — tha: x + x is two sticks taped end to end. That's 2x. A square of sticks is x·x. They are not the same.
map.Two tests, crew: distribute and combine: Two tests, crew. Distribute and combine like terms. Or substitute a number into both sides. Equivalent expressions match each time. The glitch needs you wrong just once.
map.Equivalent expressions name the same val: Equivalent expressions match for each value of the variable. One miss = not equivalent.
map.Sort the pairs, reader — true twins powe: Sort the pairs, reader. True twins power the door. Fakes feed the glitch.
map.Four panels, four pairs. Tap a panel to: Four panels, four pairs. Tap a panel to stamp it. First tap: EQUIV (true twins, equal for EVERY x). Second tap: NOT (fake). Third tap clears it. All four stamps must be right at once.
map.Conceptual: twins agree for EVERY value: Conceptual: twins match for EACH value of x. Substitute x = 1, then x = 2, into both sides. One miss shows a fake.
map.Procedural: distribute parentheses and c: Procedural: distribute and combine like terms first. Then judge. Know that a(b − c) = ab − ac. The number out front must hit BOTH terms inside. If not sure, test a number.
map.The vault's heart: a 24-tooth gear and a: The vault's heart: a gear with 24 teeth and a gear with 36 teeth. The link gear must be the greatest common factor. It is the biggest number that divides both.
map.And the timing lights blink every 6 turn: The lights blink each 6 turns and each 8 turns. They match at the least common multiple. That is the first count they share.
map.GCF: the greatest factor two numbers sha: GCF: the greatest factor two numbers share. LCM: the least number both count to. Factors divide in. Multiples count up.
map.Size the cog and set the timing, reader: Size the gear and set the time, reader. The heart won't turn without you.
map.Two locks turn the heart. Cog lock: the: Two locks turn the heart. Cog lock: the link gear's teeth is the GCF of 24 and 36. It is the greatest count that divides both gears. Timing lock: lights blink each 6 turns and each 8 turns. They first match at their LCM. After how many turns?
map.Conceptual: a GCF divides INTO both numb: Conceptual: a GCF divides INTO both numbers. So it is never bigger than either gear. You count UP TO an LCM. So it is never smaller than either blink number. Factors divide in. Multiples count up.
map.Procedural: list every factor of each ge: Procedural: list each factor of each gear's teeth. Keep the greatest one they share. Then skip count by 6s and by 8s. Stop when the lists land on the same number.
map.The cipher vault door. The glitch swells: The vault door. The glitch grows. It writes over Ada's words: 18x + 24.
map.Final boss. The lock wants 18x + 24 fact: Last boss. The lock wants 18x + 24 factored. Pull the greatest common factor out front: distributive property in reverse.
map.Then two more locks: one order-of-operat: Then two more locks. One is an order of operations code. One is a seal for equivalent expressions. Reader, make the key.
map.Boss Gate: factoring, powers, and equiva: Boss Gate: factor, powers, and equivalent expressions. All this vault taught you, in three locks.
map.BOSS GATE. Three locks. The glitch is wa: BOSS GATE. Three locks. The glitch is watching. No stress. (Some stress.)
The glitch grows over Ada's words. Three locks make the master key. Lock 1: factor 18x + 24. Put the greatest common factor out front. Lock 2: the wake-up code: 2³ × 5 − 10 ÷ 2. Lock 3: stamp the seal for equivalent expressions.
map.Conceptual: factoring runs the distribut: Conceptual: to factor, run the distributive property BACKWARD. Pull the greatest common factor out front. What stays inside must multiply back to the start. For the code: powers first. Then × and ÷ left to right. Subtraction last.
map.Procedural: Lock 1 — find the GCF of 18: Procedural: Lock 1: find the GCF of 18 and 24. Divide each term by it to fill the ( ). Lock 2: expand 2³ before all else. Lock 3: the 4 must multiply BOTH terms in the ( ).
map.Vault cleared! The Expression Engine reb: Vault cleared! The Expression Engine starts up. Each sign in the city shows true words again.
map.The glitch isn't gone — it's fixed. All: The glitch isn't gone. It's fixed. All its broken equations balance. Now it's just a neat little equals sign.
map.New distortion. Cold. Negative. To be co: A new bad pattern. Cold. Negative. To be continued…
map.Crew captain. Keeps the notebook, asks t: Crew boss. Keeps the notebook. Asks the next question. In this volume: cracked Ada's sentence for the sign press.
map.Evidence officer. Allergic to glitch mat: Proof finder. Can't stand glitch math. In this volume: caught "3⁴ = 12" at the power cells.
map.Builder and mixer. This volume: proved x: Builder and mixer. In this volume: showed x + x is two sticks, not a square. And sized the vault's link gear.
Pattern finder and puzzle game champ. In this volume: led the whole vault run. Door by door, lock by lock.
map.Fragment of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. Se: A piece of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. It can sense bad patterns. It can't do math. That's your job.
map.Quotient of fractions.Dividing by a frac: Quotient of fractions.Dividing by a fraction counts how many parts fit. 2 ÷ 1/3 = 6 thirds. Share 3/4 with 3 and each gets 1/4.
map.Exponent & power.The exponent counts rep: Exponent & power.The exponent counts repeated multiplication of the base. 3⁴ = 3·3·3·3 = 81. It is never 3 × 4.
map.Variable & coefficient.A variable stands: Variable & coefficient.A variable stands for the mystery number. A coefficient multiplies it. "5 more than 3 times n" is 3n + 5. At n = 4 it equals 17.
map.Equivalent expressions.Same value for ev: Equivalent expressions.Same value for each value of the variable. 3(x+4) = 3x+12 and 2x+5x = 7x. But 4(x−2) ≠ 4x−2. And x + x is 2x, not x².
map.GCF & LCM.GCF(24, 36) = 12 — the biggest: GCF & LCM.GCF(24, 36) = 12. The biggest shared factor. LCM(6, 8) = 24. The first shared multiple.
map.Distributive property.Multiply across th: Distributive property.Multiply each part of the sum. Or run it backward to factor: 18x + 24 = 6(3x + 4).
map.\"Two expressions that always agree are: "Two expressions that always match are one idea. It wears two coats. Find the idea." — A.V.
map.completed Volume 6: The Expression Engin: finished Volume 6: The Expression Engine. You know fraction division and exponents. You can write and evaluate expressions. You know equivalent expressions and GCF and LCM. You know the distributive property.
map.Thank you for cracking the vault with th: Thank you for cracking the vault with the crew. Volume 7 waits in the cold.
map.A different crew has 4 jars of lamp oil;: A new crew has 4 jars of lamp oil. Each torch burns 1/2 a jar. Ask: how many halves fit in 4 wholes?
map.Each jar holds 2 halves, so 4 jars hold: Each jar holds 2 halves. So 4 jars hold 4 × 2 = 8 halves. 4 ÷ 1/2 = 8 torches. Dividing by a unit fraction COUNTS the parts.
map.Sharing flips it: 2/3 of a jar split bet: Sharing is not the same. 2/3 of a jar split with 2 lamps: 2/3 × 1/2 = 1/3 of a jar each. Smaller parts, fair shares.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.How many 1/2-jar torches can be filled f: How many 1/2-jar torches can 5 jars fill?
map.A spare cell reads 2⁴. Expand it: 2 × 2: An extra cell reads 2⁴. Expand it: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2. That is four copies of the base, all multiplied.
map.The glitch's way: 2 × 4 = 8. Wrong — the: The glitch's way: 2 × 4 = 8. Wrong. The exponent repeats the base. It never multiplies it.
map.Different sentence: “2 less than 4 times: New sentence: “2 less than 4 times the number m.” "4 times m" → 4m. "2 less than that" → 4m − 2.
map.Watch the traps: 4(m − 2) subtracts BEFO: Watch for traps. 4(m − 2) subtracts BEFORE it multiplies. And 2 − 4m flips the subtraction. Word order is the code.
map.Test-run at m = 3: 4 × 3 − 2 = 12 − 2 =: Test at m = 3: 4 × 3 − 2 = 12 − 2 = 10. Multiply first. Then subtract.
map.Pair to judge: 5(x + 2) vs 5x + 10. Dist: Pair to judge: 5(x + 2) vs 5x + 10. Distribute: 5·x + 5·2 = 5x + 10. They match. True twins.
map.Pair: 2(x − 3) vs 2x − 3. Distribute: 2x: Pair: 2(x − 3) vs 2x − 3. Distribute: 2x − 6. That is NOT 2x − 3. The 2 must multiply the 3 too. Fake.
map.Pair: y + y + y vs 3y. Adding three copi: Pair: y + y + y vs 3y. Add three copies and you get 3 OF them. Twins. (Multiply three copies and you get y³. That is not the same at all.)
map.Different machine: gears of 18 and 30 te: New machine: gears with 18 and 30 teeth. Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Factors of 30: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30. Greatest shared factor: 6.
map.Its lights blink every 4 and every 10 tu: Its lights blink each 4 and each 10 turns. Skip count: 4, 8, … and 10, 20, … The lists first meet at 20. LCM = 20.
map.Sanity rails: the GCF (6) is no bigger t: Safety check: the GCF (6) is not bigger than either gear. The LCM (20) is not smaller than either blink count. If yours break this rule, you swapped them.
map.Practice key: factor 10y + 15. GCF(10, 1: Test key: factor 10y + 15. GCF(10, 15) = 5. Divide each term: 10y ÷ 5 = 2y and 15 ÷ 5 = 3. So 10y + 15 = 5(2y + 3). Distribute to check it!
map.Practice code: 3² × 2 − 8 ÷ 4. Power fir: Test code: 3² × 2 − 8 ÷ 4. Power first: 3² = 9. Then × and ÷ left to right: 9 × 2 = 18 and 8 ÷ 4 = 2. Subtract last: 18 − 2 = 16.
map.Practice seal: 3(4a + 2) = 3·4a + 3·2 =: Test seal: 3(4a + 2) = 3·4a + 3·2 = 12a + 6. The number out front multiplies BOTH terms. 12a + 2 would be a fake.
map.That's 2 × 1/3 — multiplying makes LESS: That's 2 × 1/3. Multiplying makes LESS ink, not more lamps. Division asks how many thirds FIT. Count the parts.
map.Lock A holds. Count every third-size sli: Lock A is shut. Count each third in BOTH jars. Use the bar model.
map.Lock A open! Now stamp Lock B — pick the: Lock A is open! Now do Lock B. Pick the quotient of 3/4 ÷ 3.
map.2 ÷ 1/3 = 6 lanterns lit, and each hand-: 2 ÷ 1/3 = 6 lamps lit. Each hand lamp glows on 3/4 ÷ 3 = 1/4 jar. The stairs light up. Down we go!
map.9/4 is 3/4 × 3 — that's multiplying. Sha: 9/4 is 3/4 × 3. That's multiplying. Sharing with 3 lamps makes each share smaller than 3/4.
map.3 lamps can't each get 3 whole jars out: 3 lamps can't each get 3 whole jars from 3/4 of one. Sharing makes the share smaller.
map.1/12 splits too far — that's dividing by: 1/12 cuts too far. That is dividing by 3 two times. Share the three quarter parts just once.
12 is 3 × 4. Exponents multiply again and again. Write four 3s. Multiply them all.
map.10 is 2 × 5 — glitch math! The exponent: 10 is 2 × 5. Glitch math! The exponent says multiply five 2s.
map.3⁴ = 81 and 2⁵ = 32. Both cells flare to: 3⁴ = 81 and 2⁵ = 32. Both cells light up. The glitch yells and runs deeper into the vault!
map.Cell A stays dark. Multiply the 3s one s: Cell A stays dark. Multiply the 3s one step at a time: 3, 9, 27, …
map.Cell B stays dark. Keep doubling: 2, 4,: Cell B stays dark. Keep doubling: 2, 4, 8, … five 2s in all.
map.Pick an expression first — the press nee: Pick an expression first. The press needs symbols to run.
map.3(n + 5) adds the 5 to n BEFORE tripling: 3(n + 5) adds the 5 to n BEFORE it times by 3. It says "3 times (5 more than n)". Read Ada's order again.
map.5n + 3 says '3 more than 5 times n' — th: 5n + 3 says "3 more than 5 times n". The coefficient and the constant swapped.
map.8n smashed 3 and 5 into one coefficient: 8n put 3 and 5 into one coefficient. But only the 3 multiplies n. The 5 is added after.
map.3n + 5 — and at n = 4 the press prints 3: 3n + 5. At n = 4 the press prints 3 × 4 + 5 = 17. True signs roll out!
map.27 means you added first. Multiplication: 27 means you added first. Multiply before you add. Times n by 3, THEN add.
map.Right expression! Now substitute n = 4:: Right expression! Now substitute n = 4. Multiply, then add. The press waits.
map.Every panel needs a stamp — EQUIV or NOT: Each panel needs a stamp: EQUIV or NOT.
map.3(x+4) = 3x+12 ✓ · 2x+5x = 7x ✓ · 4(x−2): 3(x+4) = 3x+12 ✓. 2x+5x = 7x ✓. 4(x−2) is NOT 4x−2. x+x is 2x, not x². The twin door opens!
map.72 is a common MULTIPLE of 24 and 36 — t: 72 is a common MULTIPLE of 24 and 36. The gear needs the greatest common FACTOR. A factor can't be more than the gears.
map.The cog slips. Which tooth counts divide: The gear slips. Which numbers divide 24 AND 36 with none left? Take the greatest one.
map.2 is the greatest common FACTOR of 6 and: 2 is the greatest common FACTOR of 6 and 8. The timing lock wants their first common MULTIPLE. Count UP, not in.
map.48 is a shared multiple, but the lights: 48 is a shared multiple. But the lights match sooner. LEAST common multiple.
map.6 + 8 = 14 isn't on either blink list. S: 6 + 8 = 14 is not on either blink list. Skip count by 6s and by 8s.
map.Lights still off-beat. Skip-count by 6s: The lights still don't match. Skip count by 6s and by 8s. Where do the lists first match?
map.Cog: GCF = 12 teeth. Timing: LCM = 24 tu: Gear: GCF = 12 teeth. Timing: LCM = 24 turns. CLUNK! The gear heart spins!
map.Lock 1 holds. The GCF is right! Now divi: Lock 1 is shut. The GCF is right! Now divide EACH term by it. 18x ÷ 6 gives the x term. 24 ÷ 6 gives the constant.
map.Lock 1 holds. Start with the GCF of 18 a: Lock 1 is shut. Find the GCF of 18 and 24 first. Then divide each term by it.
map.Lock 2 holds. Did 2³ become 6? Exponents: Lock 2 is shut. Did 2³ turn into 6? Exponents repeat: three 2s, multiplied.
map.Lock 2 holds. Don't march straight left: Lock 2 is shut. Don't just go left to right. Do × and ÷ BEFORE the subtraction.
map.Lock 2 holds. Order of operations: power: Lock 2 is shut. Order of operations: power first. Then × and ÷ left to right. Subtraction last.
map.Two locks open! Stamp the equivalence se: Two locks open! Stamp the last seal to finish the key.
map.Lock 3 holds. The 4 multiplied the 2n bu: Lock 3 is shut. The 4 multiplied the 2n but skipped the 3. Distribute to BOTH terms.
map.Lock 3 holds. 6n + 7 is not what the 4 d: Lock 3 is shut. 6n + 7 is not what the 4 does. To distribute, MULTIPLY each term by 4. Never add.
map.Lock 3 holds. The 4 reached the 3 but mi: Lock 3 is shut. The 4 got the 3 but missed the 2n. Both terms get multiplied.
map.18x + 24 = 6(3x + 4) · code 35 · seal 8n: 18x + 24 = 6(3x + 4) · code 35 · seal 8n + 12. ALL LOCKS OPEN! The Master Key turns. The Expression Engine WAKES!
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
